findings.title: Dropped Bernstein linear term invalidates the advertised unrestricted high-confidence shuffle analysis
findings.assumptions: B=4,r=2,alpha=.1,epsilon=.5,delta=.01, even n arbitrarily large, every x_i=4; independent randomized responses; grant the more conservative correct batch calibration epsilon_L=log(epsilon^2*(n/2)/(80log(4/delta))).
findings.decisive_evidence: First threshold2 has all true bits0. All s=n/2 randomized outputs1 have probability q_n^s with q_n=c/(epsilon^2*s+c), c=80log(4/delta). This forces R=1 and output1, invalid. Failure probability >=exp(-Theta(n log n)); for beta_L=exp(-L^2), theorem prescribes n=O(L), insufficient for this protocol for any fixed hidden constant.
findings.alternative_readings: Fixed beta or restricted joint delta/beta regimes are not refuted; no impossibility claim for all shuffle protocols. The local accuracy proof itself contains the omitted (1/alpha)log(1/beta) Bernstein term. Section2 p4 calls beta=1/poly(B) typically interesting, but Theorem1.4/G.6 do not impose that restriction; the counterexample targets the unrestricted theorem.
findings.core_dependency: G.3 high-epsilon simplification -> first line of proof G.6 -> Theorem1.4 headline shuffle guarantee.
findings.impact: Core derivation and proposed protocol fail for unrestricted confidence dependence. Adaptive LDP rate and lower-bound separation not refuted.
findings.correction: Retain the linear Bernstein term and separately handle without-replacement sampling and beta/delta regimes. Necessary condition n log n=Omega(log(1/beta)) for this calibrated protocol established; complete revised theorem not certified.

findings.title: Pinned BayesLearn endpoint selection always chooses the left endpoint
findings.assumptions: Positive weights, q=.5, chosen j with W(j)>=q; code uses inclusive W(j).
findings.decisive_evidence: flag=(q-W(j))/w(j)-q<=0 always. From uniform3 weights after first private y=0 at alpha=.1, weights=(4/15,1/3,2/5); intended ratio (q-W(j-1))/w(j)=.7 selects right while code flag=-.8 selects left.
findings.alternative_readings: Different heuristic might work; actual historical plot-generation commit not proven. Privacy of randomized response does not fail from this adaptive query choice.
findings.core_dependency: Empirical implementation of proposed BayeSS, not a refutation of abstract algorithm or proven score reduction.
findings.impact: Supported implementation/pseudocode mismatch; empirical magnitude unresolved.
findings.correction: Pass W(j)-w(j), the left cumulative mass; algebra verified, performance untested.

findings.title: Appendix D symmetric bitwise unary encoding uses twice the claimed local budget
findings.assumptions: Two one-hot categories, independent symmetric RR with per-bit retention e^epsilon/(1+e^epsilon); neighboring single-user input changes category.
findings.decisive_evidence: For inputs10 versus01 and output10, likelihood ratio=(p/(1-p))^2=e^(2epsilon)>e^epsilon.
findings.alternative_readings: Pinned experimental implementation requests optimized unary encoding use_oue=True, so the calculation does not establish a privacy violation in the experiments.
findings.core_dependency: Baseline description only; main scalar comparison randomizer and rates unaffected.
findings.impact: Local privacy calibration error in stated baseline, constant-factor sample complexity correction.
findings.correction: Use per-bit epsilon/2 for symmetric RR; total epsilon follows exactly.

findings.title: Output-value and interval-index quantile conventions are inconsistent
findings.assumptions: B=4,alpha=.1,q=.5, all observations1, output constrained to1..B.
findings.decisive_evidence: Every allowed m has F(m)=F(m+1)=1, hence the defined interval misses(.4,.6). Proofp8 returns j+1 after establishing bounds for j,j+1; AppendixC returnsj.
findings.alternative_readings: The conventional quantile-value predicate [F(m-1),F(m)] with F(0)=0, or gap indices0..B-1, repairs the example. Uniform indexing correction can preserve the intended objective and rates, but a short repair does not validate as-written success guarantees.
findings.core_dependency: Definitions2.2-2.4 specify the successful output required by the central statistical/empirical/shuffle guarantees; no legal output exists on the permitted all-ones dataset.
findings.impact: Core as-written success statements are unattainable on an allowed input, independently of sample size or privacy; intended adaptivity separation after consistent correction is not disproved.
findings.correction: Choose and apply a single convention consistently; value convention fixes the all-ones example analytically; full source/evaluation conversion unverified.
